about: KING UNIVERSITY (working name, owner 4 Nov 2026; was KING STUDIES): the King studied the way history studies its emperors, from 1947 to 2026. FACT items are public record. PhD hypotheses are opinions for scholars to argue, labelled as hypotheses. THE MAN IN MANNAT is a MOCKUMENTARY: every FILE is invented, every FACT box under it is real.

bazaar.title: The Storytellers' Bazaar
bazaar.lede: Qissa Khwani means the market of storytellers. For centuries caravans stopped in this Peshawar bazaar and paid men to tell stories through the night. In one small corner of it, and in a few towns of west Punjab, the men who would tell India its stories for the next hundred years were born.

people.p: Raised in Peshawar. Founder of the Kapoor dynasty and Prithvi Theatres.
Born Yusuf Khan. The Tragedy King, the first Method actor of Hindi cinema.

people.b: Kapoor Haveli, Qissa Khwani Bazaar, Peshawar · 1924
people.p: The Showman. Awaara made him a star across the Soviet Union.
Studied at Government College, Lahore. The Evergreen star.
Do Bigha Zamin, Garm Hava: the actor of the common man.
Made the television Ramayan (1987) that stopped all of India every Sunday.
Jubilee Kumar: so many of his films ran 25 weeks.
Wrote the songs of DDLJ, Pardes, Dil To Pagal Hai and Mohabbatein.
The King of Romance behind the camera. Made Darr, Dil To Pagal Hai, Veer-Zaara and Jab Tak Hai Jaan, his last film.
Poet. Wrote Chaiyya Chaiyya for Dil Se..
Bharat Kumar: the patriot of Hindi cinema.
Born a year before Partition. Superstar, then minister.

people.b: Shah Wali Qatal, Qissa Khwani, Peshawar
people.p: A Pathan and a freedom fighter in India's independence struggle. He made Delhi his home. In 1965 his son was born there: Shah Rukh Khan.

bazaar.note: In 2014 Pakistan declared the Peshawar homes of Raj Kapoor and Dilip Kumar national heritage; in 2020 the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government moved to buy them as museums.

timeline.d: The subcontinent is split in two. His father, a Pathan from Peshawar, chooses India.
Shah Rukh Khan is born on 2 November in New Delhi.
Meer Taj Mohammed Khan dies of cancer. Years later the Meer Foundation will carry his name.
Graduates in Economics from Hansraj College, Delhi University.
Doordarshan airs Fauji. He plays Abhimanyu Rai, an army commando.
His mother Lateef Fatima dies. He marries Gauri and moves to Bombay.
His first film release. Filmfare Award for Best Male Debut.
Baazigar and Darr: the hero is the villain, and India loves him.
Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge. It will play at Mumbai's Maratha Mandir for more than 1,000 weeks.
His first company, with Juhi Chawla and Aziz Mirza.
Buys the sea-facing bungalow in Bandra that becomes Mannat.
Red Chillies Entertainment, with Gauri Khan. Devdas releases.
And Main Hoon Na, Red Chillies' first production.
India's fourth-highest civilian honour.
And Kaun Banega Crorepati as host.
Buys the IPL franchise with Juhi Chawla and Jay Mehta.
Held for questioning at Newark airport in the US. He says it was because of his name.
"My name is Khan, and I am not a terrorist."
Red Chillies VFX builds India's biggest effects film of its time.

timeline.t: First IPL title · the first kiss
timeline.d: KKR win the IPL. Jab Tak Hai Jaan, Yash Chopra's last film, ends his no-kiss rule.
Named after his father; supports women survivors of acid attacks.
France makes him a Knight of the Legion of Honour. KKR win again.
He speaks about rising intolerance. Calls to boycott Dilwale; he is told to go to Pakistan.
The film fails. A silence of almost five years begins.
His family is pulled into a drugs case. In 2022 the agency drops the charges for lack of evidence.
Pathaan, Jawan, Dunki. Two of them pass ₹1,000 crore worldwide (reported).
Career award at Locarno, KKR's third title, and his first place on the Hurun India Rich List.
National Film Award for Best Actor (Jawan), his first. Met Gala debut. Hurun lists him a billionaire.
24 December 2026.

levels.name: Pre-K
levels.title: Feelings
levels.intro: Before we learn history, we learn feelings. One feeling, one character.

lessons.line: Love waits. Raj will not run away with Simran: he waits for her father's blessing.
lessons.act: Draw someone you love, and write what you would wait for.
lessons.q: In DDLJ, how does Raj want to marry Simran?
notes: In Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (1995), Raj Malhotra falls in love with Simran on a train journey across Europe. Her father, Baldev Singh, has already promised her to someone else in Punjab.

Simran is ready to run away with Raj. Raj says no. He follows her to Punjab and stays near her family until her father himself lets her go. He wants to marry her with her father's blessing, not behind his back.
That is the lesson: love is patient. It does not grab. It waits for the right way.
keys: Love waits and does not run away

lessons.line: Rahul follows Kiran everywhere and frightens her. Wanting someone so much that you scare them is not love.
lessons.act: Talk about it: how does Kiran feel?
lessons.q: Rahul in Darr scares Kiran. Is that love?
o: No, love never makes someone afraid
notes: In Darr (1993), directed by Yash Chopra, Rahul Mehra loves Kiran. But Kiran does not love him back: she loves Sunil and marries him.
Rahul will not accept no. He follows her, calls her, hides near her and frightens her family. He stammers her name: K-K-K-Kiran.
Kiran is afraid all the time. When someone you say you love is afraid of you, that is not love. Love never makes another person scared.

lessons.line: Mohan, a NASA scientist, goes back to an Indian village and gives it light.
lessons.act: Name one thing you could fix in your street.
lessons.q: What does Mohan bring to the village of Charanpur?
notes: In Swades (2004), Mohan Bhargava is a scientist at NASA in America. He comes back to India to find Kaveri Amma, the woman who looked after him as a child.
In the village of Charanpur there is no steady electricity. Mohan and the villagers build a small power station using the water of a stream, and the bulbs light up for the first time.
Good is using what you know to help other people, even when nobody asks you to.

lessons.line: Vijay hurts Shivani and her family because he wants her. Bad is hurting someone to get what you want.
lessons.act: Can a hero's face play a bad man? Look at his eyes in this picture.
lessons.q: What makes Vijay bad?
o: He hurts others to get what he wants
notes: In Anjaam (1994), Vijay Agnihotri is rich and wants Shivani, but she marries another man. Vijay ruins her family's life to punish her.
Vijay is bad because he hurts other people to get what he wants. Being rich does not make him bad; hurting people does.
The same face that played Raj and Rahul played Vijay, and he won the Filmfare award for a negative role for it. A good actor can show us what bad looks like so we can recognise it.
keys: Vijay hurts others to get what he wants
Bad is hurting someone to get your way

lessons.line: "Pyaar dosti hai": love is friendship.
lessons.act: Make a friendship band for your best friend.
lessons.q: What does Rahul say love is?
notes: In Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998), Rahul Khanna and Anjali are best friends at college. Rahul says his famous line: pyaar dosti hai, love is friendship.
Years later he understands that his best friend was the one he loved all along. A friend is someone who knows you, plays with you and stays with you.

lessons.line: He gets on the wrong train and finds the adventure of his life. Even a wrong train can take you to the right place.
lessons.act: Tell a story about a mistake that turned out well.
lessons.q: Rahul is on the wrong train. What happens?
o: He has the adventure of his life
notes: In Chennai Express (2013), Rahul Mithaiwala is supposed to carry his grandfather's ashes to Rameswaram. He means to slip away to Goa with his friends instead.
He ends up on the Chennai Express, meets Meenamma, and finds himself in the adventure of his life in her village in Tamil Nadu.
Happy is sometimes a surprise. A wrong train can take you to the right place.
keys: He has the adventure of his life

lessons.line: Aman knows his heart is weak. He spends his time making everyone around him smile.
lessons.act: Do one thing today to make someone smile.
lessons.q: Aman knows he is very ill. What does he do?
o: Makes the people around him happy
notes: In Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003), Aman Mathur lives in New York. He knows his heart is weak and he may not live long.
He does not hide or stay angry. He spends his days making the people around him happy, especially Naina and her family.
Sad things happen to everyone. What we do with our sad days is our choice.
keys: Aman knows he is very ill
He makes the people around him happy

lessons.line: A ghost falls in love and gently takes a man's shape. Not everything that looks scary is bad.
lessons.act: Draw a friendly ghost.
lessons.q: Is everything that looks scary bad?
notes: In Paheli (2005), based on a Rajasthani folk tale, a ghost falls in love with a young bride whose husband has gone away on business.
The ghost takes the husband's shape and lives with her gently and kindly. He looks scary only because he is a ghost; he is not cruel.
Not everything that looks scary is bad. Look at what someone does, not only at how they look.
keys: The ghost is gentle, not cruel

levels.aim: Name eight feelings, each through one of his characters.
outcomes: Say what love, hate, good and bad mean in your own words
Tell a scary-looking thing from a bad thing
Connect one feeling to one film and one character

levels.name: KG
levels.title: Right and Wrong
levels.intro: The same face, many choices. Every choice is a lesson.

lessons.line: His first role on television: a young commando in training. Brave is standing up for your country.
lessons.act: Salute like a soldier.
lessons.q: In Fauji, what does Abhimanyu join?
notes: Fauji (1989) was a Doordarshan serial about young men training to be commandos in the Indian Army. He played Lieutenant Abhimanyu Rai.
It was his first role on television. Brave is training hard and standing up for others and for your country.
keys: Fauji was his first TV role

lessons.line: The girls introduce themselves by their states. Kabir wants to hear only one name: India.
lessons.act: Play a game where nobody wins alone.
lessons.q: What name does Kabir Khan want his players to call their team?
notes: In Chak De! India (2007), Kabir Khan coaches the Indian women's hockey team. At first each player introduces herself by her state: Punjab, Haryana, Jharkhand, Mizoram.
Kabir does not want to hear their states. He wants one name only: India. Only when they play as one team do they start to win, and they go on to win the World Cup.
A team is many people who play for one name.

lessons.line: Rizwan walks across America to tell the President one sentence: my name is Khan, and I am not a terrorist.
lessons.act: Write your name. Say one good thing it means.
lessons.q: What does Rizwan want to tell the President?
o: That he is not a terrorist
notes: In My Name Is Khan (2010), Rizwan Khan lives in America. After the attacks of 11 September 2001 people start to fear Muslims, and his family is hurt.
Rizwan walks across the country to meet the President and tell him one sentence: my name is Khan, and I am not a terrorist.
A name tells you who someone's family is. It does not tell you if they are good or bad. Judging a person by their name is unfair.
keys: Rizwan wants to say he is not a terrorist
A name is not a verdict

lessons.line: An Indian pilot spends 22 years in a Pakistani jail and never stops loving. Love has no border.
lessons.act: Draw your home, and the people in it.
lessons.q: How many years does Veer spend in jail?
notes: In Veer-Zaara (2004), Veer Pratap Singh is an Indian Air Force rescue pilot. He loves Zaara, a girl from Pakistan.
To protect her name he stays silent and spends 22 years in a Pakistani jail. A young lawyer, Saamiya, finally tells his story in court.
Belonging is about people, not only places. Love does not stop at a border.

lessons.line: Ajay takes revenge for his family, and revenge takes him. Revenge eats the one who carries it.
lessons.act: Talk about it: when someone hurts you, what else can you do?
lessons.q: What happens to Ajay at the end of Baazigar?
notes: In Baazigar (1993), Ajay Sharma's family was ruined by a powerful man. Ajay grows up wanting revenge and does terrible things to get it.
At the end he gets his revenge, but he loses his life, dying in his mother's arms.
Revenge feels strong but it eats the person who carries it. There are other ways to answer hurt: telling the truth, asking for help, forgiving.
keys: Ajay loses his life at the end
Revenge eats the one who carries it

lessons.line: The emperor wins at Kalinga, sees the dead, and chooses peace.
lessons.act: Make a peace sign with both hands.
lessons.q: After the war of Kalinga, what did Asoka choose?
notes: In Asoka (2001), he plays the emperor Ashoka of the Maurya empire. Ashoka fights a great war at Kalinga and wins.
Walking through the battlefield he sees how many people died. He is so sorry that he gives up war and chooses peace.
History remembers Ashoka not for the war he won but for the peace he chose after it.
keys: Winning a war is not the same as being right

lessons.line: A junior artist who dreams of being a star. Want something with your whole heart and the whole universe works to give it to you.
lessons.act: Draw your biggest dream.
lessons.q: What is Om Prakash Makhija's job?
notes: In Om Shanti Om (2007), Om Prakash Makhija is a junior artist in the 1970s: one of the many extras in the background of a film. He dreams of being a big star.
He believes that if you want something with your whole heart, the whole universe helps you get it.
A dream starts small. Om starts in the background of the picture.
keys: Want it with your whole heart

lessons.line: Sent away from home, he is brought back by his little brother. Family is coming home, however long it takes.
lessons.act: Hug someone in your family.
lessons.q: Who brings Rahul back home?
notes: In Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001), Rahul Raichand marries the girl he loves and his father sends him away. Rahul goes to live in London.
Years later his little brother Rohan goes to London to find him and bring the family together again.
Family is coming home, however long it takes.
keys: Rohan, the younger brother, brings Rahul home

lessons.line: He stops a metro train and makes the powerful pay what the farmers owe.
lessons.act: Talk about it: is it fair when the strong win and the weak lose?
lessons.q: What does Azad demand when he takes the metro train?
notes: In Jawan (2023), Azad takes over a metro train in Mumbai. He asks a rich and powerful man for a huge amount of money.
The money goes to clear the loans of poor farmers who could not pay their debts.
Justice asks a question: is it fair when the strong always win and the weak always lose?
keys: Azad asks for money to clear farmers' loans

lessons.line: Dr. Jug helps Kaira by listening. It is fine to cry, and fine to talk.
lessons.act: Listen to a friend for one whole minute without talking.
lessons.q: How does Dr. Jug help Kaira?
notes: In Dear Zindagi (2016), Kaira is a young woman who is unhappy and cannot sleep. She meets Dr. Jehangir Khan, Dr. Jug, a counsellor.
He does not shout at her or give orders. He listens. Slowly she talks about her childhood and starts to feel better.
It is fine to cry and it is fine to talk. A good listener helps without saying much.
keys: Dr. Jug helps Kaira by listening
It is fine to talk about feelings

levels.aim: Learn right and wrong through ten choices his characters make.
outcomes: Explain bravery, teamwork, belonging and justice with one example each
Say why revenge harms the one who takes it
Know why a name can be judged, and why that is unfair

levels.name: Grades 1–5
levels.title: The Storytellers' Bazaar, the Map and the Timeline
levels.intro: Where did he come from? Where did the storytellers come from? Learn the map and the dates.

lessons.line: Qissa Khwani Bazaar in Peshawar: the market of storytellers. Dilip Kumar and Raj Kapoor were born there, and his father came from there.
lessons.act: Find Peshawar on a map.
lessons.q: What does Qissa Khwani mean?
notes: Qissa Khwani means the market of storytellers. It is an old bazaar in Peshawar, a city that is now in Pakistan. Traders on the road to Afghanistan stopped there, and storytellers told them tales for money.
Dilip Kumar was born near this bazaar in 1922 and Raj Kapoor in 1924. His own father came from the same neighbourhood.
In 1947 India was divided, and many families from Peshawar and Punjab came to India. Some of them became the storytellers of Hindi cinema. Read the full story in the 1947 reading room on this page.
keys: Qissa Khwani = the market of storytellers
Dilip Kumar and Raj Kapoor were born there

lessons.line: A Pathan from Peshawar, a freedom fighter for India, who made Delhi his home.
lessons.act: Ask an elder where your family came from.
lessons.q: Where was his father from?
notes: His father, Meer Taj Mohammed Khan, was a Pathan from Peshawar. As a young man he took part in India's freedom struggle against British rule.
When India was divided in 1947 he chose India and made Delhi his home. The Meer Foundation, which his son started in 2013, carries his name.
keys: A freedom fighter who chose India

lessons.line: Born on 2 November 1965, in New Delhi.
lessons.act: Draw a birthday cake with 61 candles. Count them.
lessons.q: Which city was he born in?
notes: He was born on 2 November 1965 in New Delhi. He grew up in Delhi, went to St. Columba's School and studied at Hansraj College.
In Delhi he acted in theatre before television found him. Every 2 November fans now celebrate his birthday outside his home in Mumbai.

lessons.line: Doordarshan, 1989. A boy from Delhi in an army uniform.
lessons.act: Name a TV show your parents watched.
lessons.q: What was his first TV show on air?
notes: Doordarshan was India's government TV channel, and in 1989 almost every family watched it. That year he appeared in Fauji as Abhimanyu Rai, an army commando in training.
Fauji was his first show on air. After it came Circus and other serials. Television made Indian homes know his face before cinema did.
keys: Fauji was his first show on air

lessons.line: His first film release, and his first Filmfare award.
lessons.act: Count: how many years from Deewana (1992) to KING (2026)?
lessons.q: Which was his first film to release?
notes: He moved to Bombay in 1991. His first film to release was Deewana in June 1992, in which he played Raja Sahay.
For Deewana he won the Filmfare award for Best Male Debut. From Deewana (1992) to KING (2026) is 34 years.

lessons.line: Mannat means a wish made to God. Every birthday, thousands of fans stand outside.
lessons.act: What would you name your house?
lessons.q: What is his house in Mumbai called?
notes: Mannat is his house on the sea front at Bandstand in Bandra, Mumbai. He bought it in 2001.
Mannat means a wish or a vow made to God. Every birthday, and on Eid, thousands of fans stand outside the gate and he waves to them.
keys: Mannat = a wish made to God

lessons.line: A superstar who never forgets his poor childhood friend, the village barber. A friend is a friend, however famous you become.
lessons.act: Write a letter to an old friend.
lessons.q: In Billu, what is Billu's job?
notes: In Billu (2009), he plays a superstar called Sahir Khan who comes to shoot in a small village. Billu, the village barber, was his childhood friend.
Billu is too shy to remind him. At the end Sahir tells everyone that Billu is his friend and he has never forgotten him.
keys: A friend is a friend, however famous you become

lessons.line: From Fauji to KING: 118 films and shows, one close-up each, on the Alter Egos page.
lessons.act: Pick your 3 favourite characters on the Alter Egos page.
lessons.q: Which is the newest film in the Alter Egos?
notes: From Fauji in 1988–89 to KING in 2026 he has played 118 films and shows, counted on our Alter Egos page with one close-up per character, newest first.
KING is the newest. Fauji is the oldest. Open the Alter Egos page and find your three favourites.

levels.aim: Learn where he and the storytellers came from: the map and the dates.
outcomes: Find Peshawar, Delhi and Bombay on the map and say what joins them
Give the key dates: 1965, 1989, 1992, 2001
Name his first show, first film and his house

levels.name: Grades 6–8
levels.title: The Eras
levels.intro: We learn the Mughals ruler by ruler. We learn the King era by era.

lessons.line: A Delhi theatre boy on Doordarshan. No godfather, no film family.
lessons.act: List what he did not have when he started.
lessons.q: Who directed Circus, his TV serial? (Hint: also directed Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani)
notes: From 1988 to 1991 he worked on Doordarshan. After Fauji came Circus (1989), directed by Aziz Mirza and Kundan Shah, about a travelling circus; he played Shekharan.
Aziz Mirza later directed his films Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman, Yes Boss and Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani.
He came from Delhi theatre with no godfather and no film family. Everything after this was built from zero.
keys: Circus was directed by Aziz Mirza (with Kundan Shah)

lessons.line: Every big star refused to play the villain. He took the villains and made India love them.
lessons.act: Discuss: why did audiences love him as a villain?
lessons.q: Which 1993 Yash Chopra film made him the stalker?
notes: In 1993 and 1994 he played three men who did wrong: Ajay in Baazigar (1993), Rahul in Darr (1993, directed by Yash Chopra) and Vijay in Anjaam (1994).
Many established heroes did not want such roles. He took them and audiences loved him anyway. In Darr he was the stalker who scared Kiran, and the hero began to look ordinary next to him.
This was the anti-hero era: the newcomer who broke the rule that the hero must always be good.
keys: Darr (Yash Chopra, 1993) made him the stalker

lessons.line: For ten years he ruled love. The NRI hero, the open arms, the mustard fields.
lessons.act: Make a list of five love songs of this era.
lessons.q: Which film ran more than 1,000 weeks at Maratha Mandir?
notes: From 1995 to 2004 he ruled romance. Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (1995) ran at Maratha Mandir in Mumbai for more than 1,000 weeks, the longest run of any film in India.
Then came Dil To Pagal Hai (1997), Kuch Kuch Hota Hai (1998), Mohabbatein (2000), Kal Ho Naa Ho (2003) and Veer-Zaara (2004).
This era gave the NRI hero, the open arms, and the mustard fields of Punjab.
keys: DDLJ ran 1,000+ weeks at Maratha Mandir

lessons.line: At the top of the empire he risked it: an emperor, a scientist, a ghost's lover, a disgraced coach.
lessons.act: Pick the bravest choice of this era and explain why.
lessons.q: In which film is he a disgraced hockey coach?
notes: At the top he took risks: an emperor in Asoka (2001), a NASA scientist in Swades (2004), a ghost's lover in Paheli (2005), and Kabir Khan in Chak De! India (2007).
In Chak De! Kabir is a former hockey captain disgraced after a loss to Pakistan, who comes back as coach of the women's team.
keys: Chak De!: the disgraced hockey coach

lessons.film: Om Shanti Om, Ra.One, Don 2, Chennai Express
lessons.line: Red Chillies grows: films, VFX, cricket. The actor is now the owner.
lessons.act: Draw the logo of your own company.
lessons.q: Which IPL team does he own?
notes: With his wife Gauri Khan he founded Red Chillies Entertainment in 2002. Its films grew, its visual effects company grew, and in 2008 he became co-owner of the Kolkata Knight Riders in the IPL.
Om Shanti Om (2007), Ra.One (2011), Don 2 (2011) and Chennai Express (2013) belong to this age. The actor became an owner.

lessons.film: Happy New Year, Fan, Raees, Zero
lessons.line: The darker roles, the 2015 intolerance storm, and Zero's failure.
lessons.act: Discuss: what does Fan say about fans like us?
lessons.q: In Fan, Gaurav is a fan of which star?
notes: From 2014 to 2018 the roles got darker and stranger: Charlie in Happy New Year (2014), Gaurav and Aryan Khanna in Fan (2016), Raees (2017), and Bauua Singh in Zero (2018).
In Fan he played two people: the superstar Aryan Khanna and Gaurav, the fan who looks like him and worships him.
In 2015 he spoke about intolerance in India and faced a storm. Zero (2018) did not do well.
keys: In Fan, Gaurav is a fan of Aryan Khanna

lessons.line: More than four years without a lead role. The world said he was finished.
lessons.act: Write what you think he did in those five years.
lessons.q: Which film came before the silence?
notes: After Zero (December 2018) he did not release a film as lead hero for more than four years. Many people said his career was finished.
During these years his family went through a difficult public time in 2021. He gave almost no interviews.
keys: More than four years without a lead role

lessons.line: Three films in one year. The biggest comeback in Hindi cinema.
lessons.act: Compare the three heroes of 2023.
lessons.q: Which 2023 film is about crossing borders by the 'donkey route'?
notes: In 2023 three films released in one year: Pathaan (January), Jawan (September) and Dunki (December). Pathaan and Jawan were among the biggest hits ever in Hindi cinema.
Dunki, directed by Rajkumar Hirani, is about friends from Punjab who try to reach London by the illegal 'donkey route'.
keys: Dunki is about the donkey route

levels.prereq: KS 101 The Map and the Timeline (recommended)
levels.aim: Learn his career era by era, the way history learns dynasties ruler by ruler.
outcomes: Put the eight eras in order with their years
Name one defining film for each era
Explain the silence of 2018 to 2022 and the return of 2023

levels.name: Grades 9–10 · Boards
levels.title: The Business of the King
levels.intro: How a salaried actor moved up the food chain and became the owner.

lessons.line: Paid per episode. Start where you are.
lessons.q: Where did he start?
notes: He started on television in 1988–89 with Fauji and Circus, paid per episode like any other actor.
The first rung of the food chain is selling your work for a wage. Start where you are.

lessons.line: Build the name first.
lessons.q: In stage 2, how is he paid?
notes: From Deewana (1992) to DDLJ (1995) he became a film star, paid a fee for each film.
A star's fee grows with his name. At this stage he still owns nothing; producers own the films.

lessons.line: His face becomes an asset that sells cars, cola and soap.
lessons.q: What is the asset in stage 3?
notes: From the late 1990s brands paid him to appear in their adverts: Pepsi, Hyundai's Santro, Lux soap, TAG Heuer watches and many more.
Now his face itself is an asset. It sells cars, cola and soap.

lessons.line: His first company. Its first film failed. First risk, first loss.
lessons.q: Who were his partners in Dreamz Unlimited?
notes: In 1999 he started his first company, Dreamz Unlimited, with actor Juhi Chawla and director Aziz Mirza.
Its first film, Phir Bhi Dil Hai Hindustani (2000), did not do well. First risk, first loss. Owners can lose, workers cannot.
keys: Partners: Juhi Chawla and Aziz Mirza

lessons.line: Own what you make.
lessons.q: Which was Red Chillies' first production?
notes: In 2002 he and Gauri Khan founded Red Chillies Entertainment. Its first production was Main Hoon Na (2004), directed by Farah Khan, a hit.
Now he owned the films he made, and their profits.
keys: Red Chillies' first production: Main Hoon Na

lessons.line: Own the tools, not just the story.
lessons.q: Which film built up Red Chillies VFX?
notes: For Ra.One (2011), a superhero film full of special effects, Red Chillies built up its own visual effects arm, Red Chillies VFX.
It went on to work on many other Indian films. Own the tools, not just the story.
keys: Ra.One built up Red Chillies VFX

lessons.film: KBC, Paanchvi Pass, TED Talks India
lessons.line: Diversify.
lessons.q: Which quiz show did he host in 2007?
notes: In 2007 he hosted the quiz show Kaun Banega Crorepati, then Kya Aap Paanchvi Pass Se Tez Hain? (2008) and later TED Talks India: Nayi Soch (2017).
Television kept his name in homes between films. Diversify.

lessons.line: Fandom works beyond film. Bought in 2008 for about $75 million with Juhi Chawla and Jay Mehta.
lessons.q: How many IPL titles have KKR won?
notes: In 2008 he, Juhi Chawla and Jay Mehta bought the Kolkata Knight Riders in the new Indian Premier League, for about 75 million US dollars.
KKR won the IPL in 2012, 2014 and 2024: three titles. Fandom works beyond film.

lessons.line: One brand, many countries.
lessons.q: Which is NOT a Knight Riders team?
notes: The Knight Riders brand spread to other leagues: Trinbago Knight Riders in the Caribbean, Los Angeles Knight Riders in the USA, and Abu Dhabi Knight Riders in the UAE.
There is no London Knight Riders. One brand, many countries.

lessons.line: ₹7,300 crore in 2024; a billionaire in 2025 (per Hurun). The outsider owns the system.
lessons.q: Which list counted him a billionaire in 2025?
notes: The Hurun India Rich List counted his wealth at ₹7,300 crore in 2024 and, in 2025, named him a billionaire.
The outsider from Delhi with no film family now owns a share of the system.

lessons.line: A flop is not the end. Own the return.
lessons.q: Which 2023 film did Red Chillies produce?
notes: After the silence, Red Chillies produced Jawan (2023) with him as star. Pathaan was produced by Yash Raj Films.
A flop is not the end. Own the comeback, and the comeback pays the owner.

lessons.line: 24 December 2026.
lessons.q: When does KING release?
notes: KING, directed by Siddharth Anand, is produced by Red Chillies with Marflix. It releases on 24 December 2026.
From a wage per episode in 1989 to producing his own event film in 2026: that is the food chain.

levels.aim: Follow how a salaried TV actor moved up the food chain to owner, builder and billionaire.
outcomes: Describe the twelve stages from worker to KING in order
Explain the difference between being paid and owning
Name his companies and teams and when each began

levels.name: Grades 11–12 · Streams
levels.title: Arts, Commerce, Science
levels.intro: Choose your stream. Every stream studies the same man.

lessons.line: One gesture became a nation's sign for love. Practise it in BAAHEIN KHOL.
lessons.act: Strike the pose in BAAHEIN KHOL.
lessons.q: What is the famous signature pose?
notes: Arms stretched wide, head a little to one side: the open-arms pose. It appears in DDLJ, Kuch Kuch Hota Hai and many songs after them.
One gesture became a whole country's sign for love. You can try it in our game BAAHEIN KHOL.

lessons.line: His lines are quoted like poetry: the universe that conspires, the name that is Khan, the picture that is not over yet.
lessons.act: Write your favourite line of his and why.
lessons.q: Which film has the line about the whole universe conspiring?
notes: His lines are quoted like poetry. In Om Shanti Om (2007) his character says that if you want something with your whole heart, the whole universe conspires to give it to you.
Other lines people still quote: 'my name is Khan' and, also from Om Shanti Om, 'picture abhi baaki hai, mere dost'. Literature is not only in books.
keys: The universe line is from Om Shanti Om

lessons.line: Ra.One was sold like no Indian film before: games, merch, the digital first.
lessons.act: Plan a campaign for a film you love.
lessons.q: What did the Ra.One campaign lead with?
notes: Ra.One (2011) was sold like no Indian film before it: video games, toys, merchandise and a big push online, with digital contests for fans.
It led with digital and games, years before most Indian films did.
keys: Ra.One led with digital and games

lessons.line: The Indian abroad became the market: London, New York, Dubai.
lessons.act: Name three cities outside India where his films are huge.
lessons.q: Who was the NRI hero aimed at?
notes: NRI means non-resident Indian: Indians who live abroad. DDLJ (1995), Pardes (1997) and Kabhi Khushi Kabhie Gham (2001) were made with them in mind.
London, New York, Dubai and Toronto became big markets for Hindi films. The NRI hero was aimed at Indians living abroad.
keys: The NRI hero: Indians living abroad

lessons.line: A game designer creates a villain that escapes into the real world. In 2011 it was fiction.
lessons.act: Discuss: which part of Ra.One is real today?
lessons.q: In Ra.One, what does Shekhar design?
notes: In Ra.One (2011) he plays Shekhar, a game designer who creates a video game whose villain escapes into the real world. G.One is the hero from the game.
In 2011 a thinking machine was fiction. Today artificial intelligence can write, draw and talk.

lessons.line: Machines can now copy a face, a voice and a name. Who owns his?
lessons.act: Read the Inquilaab page.
lessons.q: Which hashtag is the fans' answer?
notes: Today machines can copy a person's face, voice and name. Fans can see their star in videos he never made.
INQUILAAB is the fans' answer: #FreeMyFace, #FreeMyVoice, #FreeMyName. Read the Inquilaab page on this site.

levels.prereq: KS 301 The Business of the King (recommended)
levels.aim: Study the same man through three lenses: Arts, Commerce and Science.
outcomes: Read a gesture and a dialogue as art
Explain how a film campaign and an overseas audience work
Discuss what machines can now do with a face

levels.name: BA
levels.title: Humanity, through the Alter Egos
levels.intro: 118 characters cover almost every kind of person. Each one is a chapter of what it means to be human.

lessons.line: Love that honours family. Impact: the NRI romance template.
lessons.q: What does Raj honour in his love?
notes: Raj in DDLJ (1995) loves Simran but refuses to elope; he wins over her family first.
Impact: the NRI romance template that Hindi cinema used for the next decade. Love that honours family.

lessons.line: When love becomes fear. Impact: the hero could now be the villain.
lessons.q: Darr shows love turning into what?
notes: Rahul in Darr (1993) loves Kiran, and his love turns into fear for her.
Impact: the hero could now be the villain, and the audience could love him anyway. Darr shows love turning into fear.

lessons.line: Pride and grief, slowly. A classic tragedy for a new generation.
lessons.q: Devdas is based on whose novel?
notes: Devdas (2002), directed by Sanjay Leela Bhansali, is based on the 1917 Bengali novel by Sarat Chandra Chattopadhyay.
Devdas loses Paro through pride and destroys himself with grief and drink. A classic tragedy retold for a new generation.

lessons.line: Judged by his name. After 9/11 the line was heard around the world.
lessons.q: Rizwan has which condition?
notes: Rizwan in My Name Is Khan (2010) has Asperger's syndrome: he sees the world differently and finds people hard to read.
After 9/11 he is judged by his name. Impact: the line 'my name is Khan' was heard around the world.

lessons.line: The price of leaving home. Put the 'donkey route' into public talk.
lessons.q: Where do Hardy's friends want to go?
notes: Hardy in Dunki (2023) is a soldier who helps friends in a Punjab village who dream of going to London.
Without visas they take the dangerous 'donkey route'. Impact: it put illegal migration into public talk.
keys: Hardy's friends want to go to London

lessons.line: Coming home to build.
lessons.q: Where does Mohan work before he returns?
notes: Mohan in Swades (2004) works at NASA in America and returns to an Indian village.
He stays to build. Impact: the question every NRI asks, should I go home?

lessons.line: The junior artist who wants it all: the outsider's anthem.
lessons.q: Om Shanti Om is set first in which decade?
notes: Om in Om Shanti Om (2007) is a junior artist in 1970s Bombay. The film then jumps 30 years.
The outsider's anthem: the background extra who wants the spotlight.

lessons.line: A short man with a tall heart: a disabled hero as the lead.
lessons.q: What is Bauua's height in the story?
notes: Bauua Singh in Zero (2018) is a short man, a man with dwarfism, from Meerut. He is loud, funny and in love.
A disabled hero as the lead of a big star film.
keys: Bauua is a man with dwarfism

lessons.line: Worship that turns into possession. Fandom looking into a mirror.
lessons.act: Discuss: where does a fan's love end?
lessons.q: Gaurav looks like which star in the film?
notes: In Fan (2016), Gaurav Chandna looks like the superstar Aryan Khanna and worships him. When the star rejects him, worship turns into possession.
Fandom looking into a mirror: where does a fan's love end?

lessons.line: The protector. The film asks voters to ask questions.
lessons.q: In Jawan, Vikram is Azad's what?
notes: In Jawan (2023) he plays both Azad and Vikram Rathore. Vikram is Azad's father, a soldier betrayed by the system.
The film asks voters to question the people they vote for. The protector.

lessons.line: The small-town boy in the big city. Millions of migrants saw themselves.
lessons.q: Where does Raju come from?
notes: In Raju Ban Gaya Gentleman (1992), Raj Mathur comes from Darjeeling to Bombay to become an engineer.
Millions of migrants to big cities saw themselves in him: the small-town boy in the big city.
keys: The migrant to the big city

lessons.line: Every honest door in the city closed on him. Is a bad man born, or made? Charlie, Raees, Ajay and Azad all took the wrong road: did they choose it, or was it chosen for them?
lessons.act: Rank Charlie, Raees, Ajay and Azad from most right to most wrong, and defend your ranking.
lessons.q: What closes for Charlie, in his own line?
o: Every door to an honest living
notes: In Happy New Year (2014), Charlie says that every door to earning an honest, legal living in the city kept closing on him. So he took the other road.
Ajay in Baazigar, Raees in Raees and Azad in Jawan also break the law. Was the wrong road chosen by them, or for them?
Is a bad man born, or made? That is the question this unit leaves you with.
keys: Every door to an honest living closed on Charlie

levels.aim: Read twelve of his characters as twelve chapters of being human, and their impact.
outcomes: Describe each of the twelve human types and the film behind it
Name the impact each character had beyond the screen
Argue whether a bad man is born or made, using Charlie, Raees, Ajay and Azad

levels.name: Post Grad
levels.title: MA · MBA · MSc · M.Phil
levels.intro: Specialise. Each degree has its core paper and its ethics.

lessons.t: MA · The Muslim hero in Hindi cinema
lessons.by: Dilip Kumar to Shah Rukh Khan
lessons.line: Yusuf Khan took the screen name Dilip Kumar for his debut, Jwar Bhata (1944). Fifty years later a Khan kept his own name and became the biggest star of all.
lessons.act: Essay: what changed between 1944 and 1995?
lessons.q: What was Dilip Kumar's birth name?
notes: Muhammad Yusuf Khan was born in Peshawar in 1922. For his debut, Jwar Bhata (1944), he took the screen name Dilip Kumar, and kept it all his life.
Fifty years later a Khan kept his own name and became the biggest star of all. What had changed in India between 1944 and 1995?
keys: Dilip Kumar was born Yusuf Khan

lessons.line: Should a star sell fairness? What does a role model owe the fans who copy him? Present both sides; the student decides.
lessons.act: Debate: one side for, one against.
lessons.q: Which endorsement debate is about skin colour?
notes: Stars sell products, and fans copy stars. Some adverts have been publicly questioned: fairness creams (they tell people lighter skin is better), pan masala and elaichi brands, and online gaming.
One side: an actor is a professional and the adult viewer decides. The other: a role model owes more to the fans who copy him. Present both; you decide.
keys: Fairness creams: the skin colour debate

lessons.line: Named after his father. Supports women survivors of acid attacks.
lessons.q: Who is the Meer Foundation named after?
notes: The Meer Foundation was set up in 2013 and named after his father, Meer Taj Mohammed Khan.
It supports women who survived acid attacks: medical care, surgery, legal help and work.

lessons.t: MSc · The star and the machine
lessons.line: Can Big Tech train machines on a face without asking? The fans' revolt against celebrity persona theft.
lessons.act: Read the Inquilaab anthem.
lessons.q: What does #FreeMyFace fight?
o: Celebrity persona theft by Big Tech
notes: AI companies train machines on millions of pictures, voices and videos, often without asking the people in them.
INQUILAAB, the fans' movement on this site, says no to celebrity persona theft by Big Tech: #FreeMyFace #FreeMyVoice #FreeMyName.
keys: #FreeMyFace fights persona theft by Big Tech

lessons.line: Every 2 November the fans gather; he waves from Mannat. On his 61st he walked out at nightfall to a platform built for the moment.
lessons.act: Field study: interview one fan who has stood outside Mannat.
lessons.q: On which date do fans gather outside Mannat?
notes: Every 2 November fans gather outside Mannat in Bandra and he waves to them. The custom goes back to the late 2000s.
On his 61st birthday in 2026 he came out at nightfall to a platform built for the moment. A field study: who comes, from where, and why?

levels.aim: Specialise: identity, ethics, giving, technology and the pilgrimage to Mannat.
outcomes: Compare the Muslim star of 1944 with the one of 1995
Present both sides of an endorsement debate
Explain the fans' case in #FreeMyFace

levels.name: PhD
levels.title: The King and Power
levels.intro: Opinion papers for literature, social justice and political science scholars. Each is a HYPOTHESIS: the public record, a counter-reading, and the question you must answer. Take your position and defend it.

lessons.t: THE NAME · being called a terrorist
lessons.line: His father was a Pathan from Peshawar who fought for India's freedom and chose India. His son was held at Newark in 2009 for his name, and in 2015 an Indian politician compared him to a terrorist and told him to go to Pakistan. His films told his own story: Rizwan ('I am not a terrorist'), Kabir Khan (the Muslim captain called a traitor after a loss to Pakistan), Veer (22 years in a Pakistani jail), Pathaan (his own people's name, worn by India's spy).
lessons.counter: A star's roles are chosen by scripts and markets, not by his wounds.
lessons.ask: What does it do to a man to prove his loyalty for 35 years? Is grace a form of courage?
lessons.q: Where is Qissa Khwani Bazaar, his father's home?
notes: Public record: his father came from Qissa Khwani in Peshawar and chose India. In 2009 he was held and questioned at Newark airport in the USA; he said it was because of his name. In 2015 he was attacked by politicians after speaking about intolerance.
His films keep returning to the theme: Rizwan, Kabir Khan, Veer, Pathaan. Read this paper with the 1947 reading room and the timeline.

lessons.film: DDLJ, Dil To Pagal Hai, KKHH, Mohabbatein, Veer-Zaara
lessons.line: For twenty years India read him as Krishna: the eternal lover, the open arms, love as leela, many gopis (Simran, Anjali, Pooja, Zaara).
lessons.counter: The romantic hero is a genre, not a god.
lessons.ask: Did a Muslim man become India's Krishna? What does that say about the India of 1995–2010?
lessons.q: In Dil To Pagal Hai, what is his character's name?
notes: Krishna in Hindu tradition is the playful, loving god of the Mahabharata and the Bhagavata stories, surrounded by the gopis.
From DDLJ (Raj) through Dil To Pagal Hai (Rahul) and KKHH (Rahul) to Veer-Zaara (Veer), India watched him as the eternal lover. This paper asks whether a Muslim actor became India's Krishna.
keys: In Dil To Pagal Hai he is Rahul

lessons.t: H2 · KAMA, the poster child of desire
lessons.line: The land of the Kamasutra made him its face of desire, yet he refused to kiss on screen for twenty years. The kiss came in 2012, in Yash Chopra's last film.
lessons.counter: The no-kiss rule was personal, not a statement about India.
lessons.ask: Desire without the kiss: restraint, business, or India's own contradiction?
lessons.q: In which film did he first kiss on screen?
notes: For about twenty years he did not kiss on screen. The first kiss came in Jab Tak Hai Jaan (2012), the last film directed by Yash Chopra.
The Kamasutra was written in India; Indian cinema long avoided the screen kiss. This paper asks what desire without the kiss means.
keys: First on-screen kiss: Jab Tak Hai Jaan

lessons.t: H3 · RAM KA CHOLA, the robe he had to wear
lessons.line: After the 2015 intolerance storm, the boycott calls against Dilwale, the silence after Zero, and the 'Besharam Rang' saffron outrage before Pathaan, the lover returned wearing Ram's robe: the soldier, the protector, the patriot, and visits to Vaishno Devi before each 2023 release. Krishna became Ram.
lessons.counter: A star at 57 chooses action; faith and strategy are his own, not forced.
lessons.ask: Was the chola chosen or forced? Krishna to Ram: evolution or survival?
lessons.q: Which Pathaan song set off the saffron outrage in December 2022?
notes: Public record: the song Besharam Rang from Pathaan drew protests in December 2022 over a saffron costume. Before his 2023 releases he was reported visiting Vaishno Devi.
His 2023 heroes were a spy, a soldier and protectors. This paper asks whether the lover put on Ram's robe by choice or under pressure.
keys: Besharam Rang set off the saffron outrage

lessons.line: Public record: in 2021 his family was pulled into a drugs case; in 2022 the agency dropped the charges for lack of evidence; in 2023 the CBI registered a case against the officer who led the raid, alleging a ₹25 crore extortion demand from the family (allegations, under investigation).
lessons.counter: One officer's alleged conduct is not a system.
lessons.ask: When the state's own investigators are accused of trying to extort the country's biggest star, is the King the most powerful man in the room, or the most vulnerable?
lessons.q: In 2022, why were the charges dropped?
notes: Public record: in October 2021 his son was arrested in a drugs case. In May 2022 the agency dropped the charges against him for lack of evidence. In 2023 the CBI registered a case against the officer who led the raid, alleging an extortion demand from the family; those are allegations under investigation.
This paper asks what that record says about a star's power and his vulnerability.
keys: Charges dropped for lack of evidence

lessons.line: Dilip Kumar took a Hindu screen name. Muhammad Ali refused the draft, lost his title and came back as The Greatest. Ashoka chose dhamma after Kalinga. Shah Rukh Khan answered boycotts, silence and a family case with the biggest year in Hindi cinema, and said nothing.
lessons.ask: He never answered his critics with words, only with box office. Is silence a form of resistance?
lessons.q: Who refused the Vietnam draft and lost his title?
notes: Dilip Kumar took a screen name. Muhammad Ali refused the Vietnam War draft in 1967, was stripped of his boxing title and came back to win it again. Ashoka gave up war after Kalinga.
He answered boycotts, silence and a family case with the biggest year of his career in 2023, and said almost nothing. This paper asks whether silence can be resistance.

levels.aim: Argue the King and power: identity, myth, pressure and silence. Opinion papers, not verdicts.
outcomes: Separate the public record from the hypothesis in each paper
State the counter-reading fairly before you reject it
Take a position on every paper and defend one in a thesis of 81 words or more

mock.title: THE MAN IN MANNAT
mock.lede: In our world, the King became King through love. In this world, he was made. Every FACT box is real history. Every FILE is invented. To open the next file, you must know the real history.

files.fact: On 28 December 1895 the Lumière brothers held the first paid film screening in Paris. Within twenty years governments were making war propaganda on film.
files.file: The camera was never built for entertainment. It was built to watch. The Bureau, a society of watchers with members in every capital, gave the world cinema as a gift so that the world would sit still in the dark and look where it was told. Their first rule: [[a face on a screen moves more people than an army]].
files.q: In which city was the first paid film screening?

files.fact: Yusuf Khan, born in Qissa Khwani Bazaar, made his debut in Jwar Bhata (1944) under the screen name Dilip Kumar.
files.file: The Bureau's first lesson in faces: a nation will love a man more easily if it can [[forget where he came from]]. Yusuf became Dilip. The file notes he never forgot. Fifty years later another Khan would refuse to change his name, and the Bureau would spend thirty years [[making him pay for it]].
files.q: What was Dilip Kumar's birth name?

files.fact: The India–Pakistan border was drawn by Cyril Radcliffe, a British lawyer who had never been to India, in about five weeks. Dilip Kumar and Raj Kapoor were born in Peshawar's Qissa Khwani, the Storytellers' Bazaar.
files.file: In this history, the line was not drawn by a lawyer. It was drawn by the Bureau, around one bazaar. They had studied the Storytellers' Bazaar for a century: no place on earth bred more men who could make a crowd cry. Operation Qissa moved the storytellers to Bombay to become the faces of a new nation. One storyteller's son refused to go to Bombay. He was a Pathan, a freedom fighter, and he kept [[a list of every name the Bureau had moved]]. He settled in Delhi. Codename: MEER.
files.q: Who drew the India–Pakistan border in 1947?

files.fact: J. Edgar Hoover's FBI kept a large file on Charlie Chaplin. In 1947 the Hollywood Ten were blacklisted. In 1952 Chaplin's re-entry permit to the United States was revoked while he was at sea.
files.file: Hoover did not watch the actors. He ran them. Every star in Hollywood was an asset; the blacklist was the list of those who said no. Chaplin said no, and the Bureau [[closed the door behind his ship]]. The Bureau learnt a second rule: you cannot kill a famous man, but you can [[close every door]].
files.q: In which year was Chaplin's re-entry permit revoked?

files.fact: Raj Kapoor's Awaara (1951) became a phenomenon in the Soviet Union. In the same decade the CIA secretly funded the animated film of Animal Farm (1954).
files.file: Both sides of the Cold War used films. The Bureau used Bombay as the only neutral studio on earth. Raj Kapoor's songs crossed the Iron Curtain carrying [[messages nobody could stop, because everybody was singing them]]. That is why, in this history, the song sequences were always shot abroad: [[every song abroad was a handover]].
files.q: Which Raj Kapoor film became huge in the Soviet Union?

files.fact: Shah Rukh Khan was born on 2 November 1965 in New Delhi. His father died in 1981.
files.file: MEER had a son. The Bureau watched him from the cradle: a Pathan's son from the Storytellers' Bazaar, born in the capital of the country his father chose. When MEER died in 1981, the list [[passed to the boy]]. He was fifteen.
files.q: In which year did his father die?

files.fact: In 1989 Doordarshan aired Fauji, in which he played Abhimanyu Rai, a commando in training.
files.file: The Bureau's recruitment programme, broadcast as a TV serial. The cadet's codename was ABHIMANYU, from the Mahabharata: the warrior who knew how to enter the chakravyuh, the deadly spiral formation, but [[not how to get out]]. The Bureau chose the name on purpose. They trained him to enter. Nobody taught him the way out.
files.q: In Fauji, what was his character's name?

files.fact: In 1993 he played killers and stalkers in Baazigar and Darr; audiences made him a star.
files.file: Bureau experiment 93/B: will a nation love the face of a villain? Result: yes. The report, marked [[most dangerous finding in the Bureau's history]], concludes that this face can make a crowd love anything, even its own fear. The order goes out: [[make him the lover. Never let him be the villain again]].
files.q: In which 1993 film did he play a stalker?

files.fact: Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge (1995) played at Mumbai's Maratha Mandir for more than 1,000 weeks.
files.file: The longest-running operation in Bureau history. Objective: bind the Indians abroad to home through one love story. It worked too well. The Bureau lost control of the film: the fans [[would not let it leave the cinema]]. For the first time the faces belonged to the crowd, not the Bureau.
files.q: Where did DDLJ play for more than 1,000 weeks?

files.fact: In 2001 he bought the sea-facing bungalow in Bandra that became Mannat. Every 2 November thousands of fans gather outside.
files.file: The Bureau thought Mannat was a safehouse. It was a fortress of another kind: the only building in the world the Bureau cannot get near, because [[every birthday the crowd outside becomes a wall]]. The man in Mannat keeps MEER's list there. The balcony wave, the file says, is [[a signal to the fans]].

files.fact: In August 2009 he was held for questioning at Newark airport in the US; he said it was because of his name.
files.file: The Bureau's allies held him for two hours. Officially: his name was on a list. In the file: [[they were looking for MEER's list]]. They searched his luggage. They did not find it. The list was never on paper. [[He had learnt it by heart]].
files.q: At which airport was he held in 2009?

files.fact: In Ra.One (2011) a video-game villain made of code escapes into the real world. Red Chillies VFX built its effects.
files.file: A briefing disguised as a blockbuster. In 2011 he told a billion people what the Bureau was building: a machine that takes faces. The villain was RA.ONE. The hero, G.ONE, was [[the fans' firewall]]. Most people saw a superhero film. The ones who understood [[started a movement]].
files.q: In Ra.One, where does the villain come from?

files.fact: After Zero (2018) he had no lead release for almost five years. In 2021 his family was pulled into a case whose charges were dropped in 2022 for lack of evidence.
files.file: The Bureau's last move, from rule two: [[close every door]]. Five years of closed doors. The file on these years is mostly blacked out. One line survives: [[he did not break]].
files.q: Which film came just before the silence?

files.fact: In 2023 he released Pathaan (a spy), Jawan (a man who hijacks the system to pay farmers' debts) and Dunki (border-crossers on the donkey route).
files.file: Decoded, the three films of 2023 are one message to the fans in three parts: [[the spy knows]] (Pathaan), [[the system can be stopped]] (Jawan), [[the border was always a line someone drew]] (Dunki). The Bureau understood too late. The crowd was already singing.
files.q: Which 2023 film is about the donkey route?

files.fact: Machines can now copy a face, a voice and a name. Fans launched INQUILAAB: #FreeMyFace #FreeMyVoice #FreeMyName.
files.file: The Bureau's newest weapon copies faces without asking. The last line of MEER's list is not a name. It is three words: [[FREE MY FACE]]. In the bazaars of this world, people pass around a forbidden reel. It shows another history, one where there was no Bureau, and a storyteller's son from Delhi became King by nothing but [[love, work and the fans]]. They say it is only a story. You are living in it. File 016, KING, opens on 24 December 2026.
files.q: What are the three hashtags of the Inquilaab?
